main_text.p: dimidia pars eius precij in re uendita, tradita est. In summa, fraudatio supra dimidiū ueri precij admissa dicitur, cū aut pecunia dimidiū rei, aut res dimidium pecuniæ non ualet. De iure, satis iam à nobis explicatum uidetur. nunc ad eas controuersias, quæ ex scripto pariuntur, transeundum est: quarum triplicē esse rationem, superius dicebamus. eas enim aut ex scripti ambiguitate, aut ex scripti sententiēque[?] diffensione, aut ex contrariè scriptis manare.
Scripti ergo ambiguitas controuersiam efficit, cùm (ut Cornificius ait) scriptū duas

page.notes: Left margin annotations are manuscript handwriting and are not printed text; they are omitted. The running head at the top is too worn to read reliably. "sententiēque" is uncertain in its macron and marked [?]. The word "aut" at the lower right is treated as the catchword, not as text.
